written.q: Define prompt engineering and explain five reasons it is important.
written.a: Prompt engineering is the process of creating clear and effective inputs for an AI system to guide it toward the desired output. Important because it improves accuracy by reducing vague or irrelevant responses, saves time (useful results in fewer attempts), enhances creativity, supports problem solving by guiding the AI through logical steps, and increases reliability in summarisation, coding and analysis.

written.q: Explain the TRADE framework and rewrite 'Write an email about saving money' using it.
written.a: TRADE = Task (what, with an action verb), Role (who the AI acts as), Audience (who reads it), Details (length, format, tone, constraints), Example (a sample output, i.e. few-shot). Rewrite: Role: You are a friendly finance coach. Task: Write a short email with 3 tips to save money on groceries. Audience: busy college students. Details: under 150 words, casual tone, bullet points. Example: format as 'Tip 1: [Catchy Name] - [one-sentence action]'.

written.q: Describe the five prompting techniques with an example of each.
written.a: Zero-shot: a task with no examples ('Classify this review as positive or negative'). Few-shot: a few solved examples first. Chain-of-thought: ask for step-by-step reasoning ('Think step by step'). Role prompting: assign a role ('Act as a teacher'). Constraint-based: add rules ('Explain in 100 words').

written.q: State the best practices and limitations of prompt engineering.
written.a: Best practices: use simple and direct language, provide enough context, specify the expected output format, avoid ambiguous or overly broad instructions. Limitations: responses may contain errors or outdated information; poorly designed prompts can lead to biased, incomplete or irrelevant outputs; it does not guarantee perfect results.

written.q: Using the AI Kitchen analogy, explain prompt, context, harness and loop engineering.
written.a: Prompt: the clear order given to the chef. Context: the company recipe book placed beside the chef (in AI, RAG supplies the right documents so the model does not hallucinate). Harness: the safe prep station, approved tools and fire extinguisher (in AI, sandboxed infrastructure and tools such as APIs and file systems). Loop: act, observe, evaluate, loop and terminate quality control (in AI, an agent checks its own work against tests and self-corrects, e.g. with LangGraph).
